samples: This module defines circles, rectangles, and points, computes their areas, and produces short human-readable descriptions of them. It can also select the shape with the largest area from a list, returning nothing for an empty list. Its main program prints descriptions for a few sample shapes and then prints which one is largest.

This module defines circle, rectangle, and point shapes, computes their areas, and formats a short text description for each. It can also pick the shape with the greatest area from a list, returning nothing for an empty list. Its main function prints descriptions of a small sample set and identifies the largest one.

This module models simple plane shapes—circles, rectangles, and points—with positive dimensions where applicable, and can compute their areas. It provides functions to describe a shape with its rounded area and to select the shape with the largest area from a list, returning nothing for an empty list. Its main program prints descriptions for a small built-in sample and reports the largest one.

This module defines circles, rectangles, and points, computes their areas, describes them in readable text, and can find the shape with the largest area from a list. Its `main` function prints descriptions of a few sample shapes and then prints which one is largest. Use it if you need simple area measurement and summaries for basic plane shapes.

This module defines circles, rectangles, and points, can compute their areas, describe them in text, and find the shape with the largest area in a list. Its command-line entry point prints descriptions for a small built-in set of sample shapes, then prints which one is largest. Use it if you need simple positive-dimension shape modeling with area-based reporting.
